subject: AcmePay onboarding: SDK setup, traffic smoothing & rate handling
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AcmePay onboarding: SDK setup, traffic smoothing & rate handling

Hi Sarah —

Great to kick this off. Per our call last week I'm pulling together a compact plan to get your integration live with minimal risk and predictable costs. Attached: acmepay_mutual_action_plan.pdf (timeline & owners) and a tiny SDK patch with sample wiring (sdk_sample.patch).

High-level, proposed approach:
- Week 0 (this week): integration workshop + sandbox validation (1.5h)
- Week 1: enable traffic smoothing + KV cache alignment; run smoke load tests
- Week 2: canary cutover of 10% traffic -> 50% -> full with monitoring gates

Specific asks for your team ahead of the workshop:
1) Confirm who will run smoke tests (engineer + test account)
2) Share expected peak RPS and typical burst profile (1h, 6h windows)
3) Any procurement constraints around IP allowlists or vendor terms

I'll schedule a 60–90m workshop; proposed slots Wed Jul 7 at 10am PT or Thu Jul 8 at 2pm PT. Which works?

Thanks — I want to make this low-friction for your eng team.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments: acmepay_mutual_action_plan.pdf, sdk_sample.patch

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmepay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcmePay Procurement <procurement@acmepay.com>
Date: 2026-07-04T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay onboarding: SDK setup, traffic smoothing & rate handling

Thanks Vanessa — Wed Jul 7 at 10am PT works for our team. I'll invite Mark (backend lead) + procurement.

Quick question ahead of the workshop: our traffic pattern includes a daily spike around 11am ET with short 2–3 minute bursts (10x baseline). We need to be sure any client-side retries and Redwood's rate controls won't cause a 429 cascade or increase cost unexpectedly. Does Redwood provide guidance or a default guardrail for per-tenant burst handling and graceful degradation?

Also procurement asked for a short summary of cutover steps so they can plan approvals. Can you include that in the workshop agenda?

Cheers,
Sarah
Head of Integrations, AcmePay

From: Mark Thompson <mark.t@acmepay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmepay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-04T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay onboarding: SDK setup, traffic smoothing & rate handling

On Sat, Jul 4, 2026 at 14:30 Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Operational knobs we suggest enabling during cutover:
> - KV prefix caching for repeated prompts (saves CPU and tokens)
> - Adaptive batching (start at batchSize: 4; monitor latency and increase if stable)
> - Traffic smoothing layer in front of the SDK to shape short bursts into a steady flow for 30s windows

Thanks Monica — that helps. A couple clarifications:
1) We currently call the endpoint at /v1/generate from multiple services. Is it safe to publish /v2/generate in parallel and route only a subset of traffic, or do we need to maintain header translation?
2) What's your recommended DNS TTL for the canary to allow quick rollback? Our infra team prefers not to touch DNS mid-cutover.
3) Can you confirm exactly which metrics will be used as monitoring gates (I want to list them in our runbook): error rate (5xx), 95p latency, and token spend variance? Anything else we should include?

If we can answer those I can sign off to procurement for a 3-week accelerated cutover window.

— Mark
Senior Backend Engineer, AcmePay

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Thompson <mark.t@acmepay.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-04T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay onboarding: SDK setup, traffic smoothing & rate handling

Thanks Mark — quick consolidated answers and next steps so procurement has what they need for sign-off.

Answers:
- Parallel /v2 in front of /v1: yes — deploy /v2 and use feature-flagged routing. No header translation required if you keep the same auth contract; if payload changes, we recommend a tiny shim in the routing layer to normalize.
- DNS TTL: keep DNS untouched. Use routing rules at the gateway/load‑balancer for traffic weights (recommended). If DNS must be used, set TTL <= 60s but gateway is preferred.
- Monitoring gates (we will include in the canary dashboard):
  * 5xx error rate (gate: < 0.5% over 30m window)
  * 95th percentile latency (gate: <15% variance vs baseline)
  * Token spend variance (gate: <20% delta)
  * Queue depth / backlog metric (gate: no sustained queue >200 for 30s)

Pre-cutover smoke checklist (owners):
- Engineering (Acme): verify SDK patch in sandbox, run 30m load at expected peak (Mark)
- Redwood Impl (Monica): enable KV cache + adaptive batching in staging and validate latency impact
- CS (Vanessa): confirm monitoring dashboards and escalation contacts are live
- Ops (Grace): confirm auto-scale thresholds and canary rollback playbook

Proposed workshop agenda (Wed Jul 7, 10am PT):
- 10m: Introductions & roles
- 15m: Review mutual action plan (timeline + approvals)
- 25m: Technical deep dive (Monica) — SDK wiring, retries, timeouts
- 20m: Cutover runbook & canary gates (Grace)
- 10m: Q/A and next steps

Next steps (action items):
1) Mark to run baseline smoke tests and post peak RPS numbers (due Mon Jul 5 COB)
2) Vanessa to send calendar invite for Wed Jul 7 10am PT (sending now)
3) Monica to upload rate_limit_matrix.csv and quick test harness link to the HubSpot Deal (done)

If that looks good I will share the workshop invite and the mutual action plan with procurement.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acmepay_mutual_action_plan.pdf, rate_limit_matrix.csv
